title: Regular pullback of dimension functions by fibre local dimension
statement: Let $r:P\to X$ be a regular morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes [def-exc-excellent-ring], meaning flat with fibres that remain regular after every finite residue-field extension [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $\delta_X:|X|\to\mathbf Z$ be a dimension function: its value drops by one along every immediate geometric specialization, where immediate means codimension one in the strict localization [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $b_r(u)=\dim\mathcal O_{P_{r(u)},u}$. Then the function $\delta_P:|P|\to\mathbf Z$ defined by $\delta_P(u)=\delta_X(r(u))-b_r(u)$ is a dimension function on $P$. No finite-type or finite-presentation hypothesis on $r$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XIV, Proposition 2.5.4, printed pp.217–218: regular pullback of dimension functions.

proof.text: It suffices to test the proposed function after every strict localization of $P$, by [lem-per-dimension-functions-strict-localization]. Fix a geometric point $\bar u$ of $P$ and its image $\bar x$ in $X$. By [lem-per-regular-strict-local-model] the induced map $f:Y=P_{(\bar u)}\to S=X_{(\bar x)}$ is local and regular between Noetherian excellent strictly local schemes, and its local fibre dimensions agree with the original ones at every point. By [lem-per-dimension-functions-strict-localization], $d_S=\delta_X\circ|S\to X|$ is a dimension function. Thus the pullback of the proposed function is $d_S(f(y))-b_f(y)$. Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$. The map $A\to B$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism] applied at the closed point.

source.place: XIV, Proposition 2.5.4, first reduction; XVII, strict-local reductions preceding Lemma 4.3.2.3.

proof.text: Choose a dimension function $d$ on $Y$ using [lem-per-local-dimension-function-calculus]. We will use the following direct chain computation for $S$ and $Y$: if $v\rightsquigarrow w$ is a Zariski specialization, then $d(v)-d(w)=\dim\mathcal O_{\overline{\{v\}}_{\mathrm{red}},w}$ (and the same formula for $d_S$). Indeed, excellence gives the bounded saturated-chain property in [def-exc-excellent-ring]; choose a saturated chain in the indicated local closure. Each consecutive pair is Zariski immediate and hence geometric immediate by [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion], so each difference is one. Summing gives its length, which is the displayed dimension by catenarity. The length-zero case gives zero.

source.place: XIV, Theorem 2.2.1, proof of Lemma 2.2.5, and Proposition 2.1.4.

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the affine fibre with ring $F_{\mathfrak p}=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is integral. To see this using precisely [lem-per-strict-local-regular-integral-fibres], extend $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ to an algebraically closed field $K$. That node says that $\operatorname{Spec}(F_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}K)$ is nonempty and integral. The ring map $F_{\mathfrak p}\to F_{\mathfrak p}\otimes K$ is injective: choose a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-linear functional $K\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ taking $1$ to $1$, whose tensor with the identity is a left inverse. Hence $F_{\mathfrak p}$ is a nonzero subring of a domain and is itself a domain. This proves integrality only for this local morphism of strict localizations.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.3; descent of the affine domain condition along a field extension is the displayed linear retraction.

proof.text: Put $C_{\mathfrak p}=B/\mathfrak pB$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] it is flat over the domain $A/\mathfrak p$, and by [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] multiplication by each nonzero element of $A/\mathfrak p$ is injective on it. Consequently its map to its localization $F_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective: an element in the kernel is killed by one such nonzero scalar, so is zero. Step 3 shows that $C_{\mathfrak p}$ is a domain. Thus $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak pB$ is a prime of $B$, contracting to $\mathfrak p$ (a nonzero scalar cannot kill $1$ in $C_{\mathfrak p}$). It is the unique generic point of the fibre. In particular $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak mB$ is prime.

source.place: Algebraic expansion of XIV Proposition 2.5.4, fibre-generic points; Stacks 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change) and the flat-domain torsion-free implication.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the flat map of Noetherian rings $A/\mathfrak p\to C_{\mathfrak p}$ and the prime $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak pB$. Its contraction is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p$; the localized source is $A/\mathfrak p$. The local closed fibre is $(B/\mathfrak mB)_{(0)}=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak mB)$, a field, so has dimension zero. The formula gives
$$\dim(C_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak pB}=\dim(A/\mathfrak p).$$
All quotients are Noetherian, and the primeness and flatness needed here were established in step 4. No finite-type assumption has entered.

source.place: Tag 00ON, lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total, applied after quotient by the base prime.

proof.text:
Apply the chain computation of step 2 to $\mathfrak p\rightsquigarrow\mathfrak m$ in $S$ and $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}\rightsquigarrow\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak m}$ in $Y$. Their reduced local closures have dimensions $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)$ and $\dim(C_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak pB}$, equal by step 5. Subtracting the two differences therefore gives
$$d_S(\mathfrak p)-d(\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p})=d_S(\mathfrak m)-d(\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak m}).$$
This proves the needed constancy at the fibre-generic points without presupposing the specialization-geometry node, whose proof depends on this item.

source.place: XIV, Proposition 2.5.4, comparison at fibre-generic points; explicit subtraction using steps 2 and 5.

proof.text:
Let $\mathfrak q$ be any prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$. It contains $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak pB$. Its reduced local closure from this generic point is $(C_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak q/\mathfrak pB}=B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], this is the local ring of the fibre at $\mathfrak q$: the maximal ideal of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ generates exactly $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$. Its dimension is $b_f(\mathfrak q)$. The chain computation in step 2 gives
$$d(\mathfrak q)=d(\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p})-b_f(\mathfrak q).$$
The displayed ring identification also follows directly by successive localization of the quotient, as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: XIV, Proposition 2.5.4, constancy on each fibre; local ring identification is Stacks Tag 0HA1, lemma-local-ring-fibre, schemes.tex lines 3544–3563.

proof.text:
For every $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, steps 6 and 7 yield
$$d_S(\mathfrak p)-b_f(\mathfrak q)=d(\mathfrak q)+d_S(\mathfrak m)-d(\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak m}).$$
The right side is a dimension function, since adding a fixed integer to $d$ preserves the decrease by one along every immediate geometric specialization. Thus the proposed function pulls back to a dimension function on every strict localization of $P$. The converse implication of [lem-per-dimension-functions-strict-localization] proves the assertion on $P$. If $P$ is empty the condition is vacuous; the length-zero and zero-dimensional fibre cases are included in these identities.

source.place: XIV, Proposition 2.5.4, conclusion by the constant difference with a dimension function.

proof_origin.place: XIV Proposition 2.5.4, printed pp.217–218, with XVII Lemma 4.3.2.3. Agent-written algebraic expansion of the same strict-local, fibre-generic comparison, replacing the last Hauptidealsatz calculation by Stacks 00ON on A/p -> B/pB.
